PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 5:05 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council recessed to Closed Session at 5:05 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council reconvened to Open Session at 6:14 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items #1 and #2.  Staff provided presentation, the City Council  provided feedback and no reportable action was taken on items #1 and #2.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:15 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE City Manager Cisneros led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Altamirano offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

2.. Presentation - National Breast Cancer Awareness Month in the City of Commerce Social Services Coordinator Garcia provided an introduction and facts related to National Breast Cancer Awareness Month.  Council Members and the Mayor encouraged all women to take preventive measures.
Mayor Rebollo asked that breast cancer survivors are honored at the next City Council meeting.  

4.. Library Update on Park Pass Grant: Storywalk Silvia Cisneros, Senior Librarian, provided an overview of the grant received -Park Pass Grant from California State Library. According to Ms. Cisneros, 20 passes received to check out for any library patron for two weeks to use. The new concept that the library is also introducing is the Story Walk. Council Members recommended providing a good outreach and informing residents about available State Park passes. 

1.. Recognition of the Commerce Dance Teams for their Achievements during 2022 Mayor Rebollo thanked all team members and coaches, and stated that the performance during the City's Birthday celebration was outstanding.  

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoya spoke for the record. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Councilmember Altamirano asked to pull item #8, and Councilmember Garcia asked to pull item #9 for discussion. 

Item #8 - Councilmember Altamirano asked whether the rendering could be presented to the Beautification Committee before the final approval. According to Acting Public Works Director Nila, the rendering will be designed and presented to the Beautification Committee, and the construction/installation will be about six months out. 
Councilmember Altamirano moved, seconded by Vice Mayor Argumedo, to approve the Resolution awarding a Professional Services Agreement to Hirsch & Associates, Inc. for the S. Eastern Ave. at SB I-5 Freeway Raised Island Beautification Project for design and coordination and authorizing project Management Services by Transtech Engineering, with the addition of the concepts and sending concepts to the Beautification committee before going to construction. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5)

Item #9 - A discussion took place about the ability to transfer the blue curb to a family member and what notifications are mailed to the applicants. The additional change included an original review by the Traffic Commission, an appeal by the Traffic Commission, and a third step of the appeal being reviewed by the City Council.

Vice Mayor Argumedo moved, seconded by Councilmember Altamirano, to adopt a Resolution approving amendments to the Blue Curb Policy. The motion was carried by the following vote: 


AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5)


7.. Update on Environmental Assessment and Remediation located at 1350 S. Eastern Avenue, Commerce

8.. Professional Services Agreement with Hirsch & Associates, Inc. for South Eastern Ave at SB I-5 Freeway Raised Island Beautification Project

9.. Blue Curb Policy Amendment

6.. Approval of Minutes

5.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 6A, 6B and 6C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

11.. Update on the New Route 500 from Transportation and the Senior Shuttle from Parks and Recreation Transportation Director McFerguson announced launching Purple Route 500. According to Director McFerguson, there were 75 passengers utilizing the new route yesterday on the day of the official launch. 
Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz provided an update on the senior shuttle launching. The number of passengers is increasing, especially on dates seniors have meetings. 

Discussion took place about the Dial-a-Ride program and wait time for the seniors. It was recommended that staff accommodate seniors or residents with limited mobility. 

According to Transportation Director McFerguson, flyers were disseminated, and information regarding the route was sent to residents and issued at shopping centers. Councilmember Lainez recommended that the follow-up survey is implemented to see if riders are satisfied with the new route. 

Councilmember Garcia recommended splitting the route as the entire route takes over an hour. It was a consensus among the City Council to bring this item back for discussion. 



10.. Sheriff’s Presentation/Update Regarding Public Safety In the City of Commerce City Attorney Tapia asked the City Council to continue item #14 to the next City Council meeting.  

Councilmember Lainez moved, seconded by Councilmember Altamirano, to continue item #14 to the next City Council meeting.  The motion was carried by the following vote: 
AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5)

Sergeant Duarte provided statistics for the last two weeks.

ORDINANCES

13.. Introduction for First Reading, by Waiving the Full Reading and Reading by Title only an Ordinance Amending Commerce Municipal Code, Title 19 (Zoning), Chapter 19.11 (Manufacturing Zones) and Table 19.11.030(A) (Uses in Industrial Districts) to Add Additional Requirements for Funeral Services and Crematory Land Uses  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Director of Economic Development and Planning Jimenez provided an overview of the staff report.  Mayor Rebollo opened public hearing.  There were no individual wishing to speak on this item.  Mayor Rebollo closed Public Hearing.  

14.. Introduction for First Reading, by Waiving the Full Reading and Reading by Title only an Uncodified Ordinance Approving a Development Agreement Related to Application No. 18-004 This item was continued to the next City Council meeting. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Lainez stated that a catalytic converter was stolen from his car and asked for an update regarding the catalytic converter ordinance the City was looking to implement. Councilmember Lainez asked for an update regarding Black Friday preparations, traffic control, and the installation of lights on Eastern Avenue. 

Councilmember Lainez stated that based on his conversation with a couple of Planning Commissioners, he would like to get an update on General Plan and what the cost would be for community meetings proposed by MIG. Councilmember Lainez reported that he attended the Clean Air Day event at Rosewood park, the Brenda Villa event last Friday, and Concert in the Park. 

Councilmember Garcia reported that she attended a Concert in the park. 

Vice Mayor Argumedo reported that he attended the Commerce United Soccer banquet, the California Clean Air Day event at Rosewood park, the Hispanic Heritage celebration, and Concert in the Park. Vice Mayor Argumedo announced that the Shurr High School placed first in water polo and congratulated the team and Commerce team residents on this prestigious achievement. 

Mayor Rebollo reminded residents about upcoming events, including Halloween celebrations. Mayor Rebollo adjourned the meeting in memory of women that lost their fight to breast cancer.
